findings.title: Invalid Ruby syntax prevents existing-topic embeds from rendering
findings.description: `<%- end if %>` contains a trailing `if` without a condition. The generated Ruby template cannot compile, so `/embed/best` fails when an existing topic is found. Replace it with `<%- end %>` and add a controller test that renders the actual view; the current controller specs only mock `TopicView`.

findings.title: Imported HTML bypasses sanitization on the forum origin
findings.description:
Returning `raw` directly bypasses the normal sanitizing cooking pipeline. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` passes decoded feed HTML into `TopicEmbed.import`, which only parses and rewrites URLs before creating a `raw_html` post. Nokogiri parsing does not remove scripts, event-handler attributes, or unsafe URL schemes, allowing malicious feed markup to become stored executable content on the forum origin.

This bypass also persists on ordinary edits: `PostsController#update` revises the raw body without changing `cook_method`, and `Guardian#can_edit_post?` permits the owning account to edit imported posts even if it is not staff. Sanitize HTML on every cooking operation, including subsequent edits, rather than treating the rendering mode as a permanent trust grant.

findings.title: Feeds without a content element abort polling
findings.description:
`i.content.scrub` assumes every feed item has a content element. Valid RSS feeds commonly provide article text through `description` or `content:encoded` instead; when `i.content` is absent, this raises rather than importing the item. Because the exception occurs inside the loop, subsequent entries are not processed either.

Select from the supported content fields, handle missing bodies explicitly, and test polling against representative RSS and Atom fixtures.

findings.title: Relative URL conversion leaves common article links broken
findings.description:
`absolutize_urls` only handles values beginning with `/`, so document-relative URLs such as `images/photo.jpg` and `../article` remain relative to the forum page instead of the source article. It also incorrectly rewrites protocol-relative URLs: `//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg` becomes a path on the article’s host.

Resolve references against the complete article URL using URI resolution semantics, and cover document-relative, root-relative, and protocol-relative references in the model specs.
